description: A single-panel stacked bar chart summarising yield-strength contributions. The y-axis is labelled "Yield strength (MPa)" with tick marks from 0 to 1400 in steps of 200; the x-axis carries four sample labels, "3Cr", "2Ni", "2Ni3Cr" and "2Ni5Cr". A legend defines five entries: σ_prep (yellow, top segment), σ_ss (purple, largest middle segment), σ_gb (green, lower-middle segment), σ_0 (orange, thin basal segment), and "experimental yield strength" shown as brown spheres with a lighter highlight. Each bar stacks the four calculated mechanism contributions from bottom to top as σ_0, σ_gb, σ_ss, σ_prep; the purple σ_ss segment is by far the tallest in every bar, indicating solution strengthening dominates the calculated total, while the orange σ_0 segment is only a thin sliver at the base. The total calculated heights rise from 3Cr to a maximum at 2Ni, then fall slightly for 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr. A single brown sphere sits above each bar, marking the tensile-test measured yield strength; all four spheres lie above their corresponding bar tops, so the experimental values exceed the summed calculated contributions, most notably for 2Ni near 1200 MPa. No numeric values are printed on any segment, bar top or data point.

observations.observation: The figure is a stacked bar chart with four bars labelled 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr along the x-axis.
The y-axis is labelled 'Yield strength (MPa)' and is scaled from 0 to 1400 with major ticks every 200 MPa.
The legend defines four strengthening contributions - σ_prep (yellow), σ_ss (purple), σ_gb (green) and σ_0 (orange) - plus 'experimental yield strength' plotted as a brown sphere.
Within every bar the purple σ_ss segment is the tallest segment, i.e. solution strengthening provides the largest share of the calculated yield strength for all four samples.
The orange σ_0 segment is only a thin sliver at the base of each bar, making the smallest contribution of all four mechanisms.

The total calculated bar height is greatest for 2Ni (its top lies between the 1000 and 1200 MPa gridlines) and is slightly lower for 2Ni3Cr, 2Ni5Cr and lowest for 3Cr (top just under the 1000 MPa gridline).

One brown sphere is plotted above each bar, marking the measured tensile yield strength; for 2Ni the sphere lies above the 1200 MPa gridline, and the spheres for 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr lie between 1000 and 1200 MPa.
All four experimental data points sit above the top of their corresponding stacked bars, so the measured yield strength exceeds the summed calculated mechanism contributions in every sample.
The green σ_gb segment is thicker in the 2Ni5Cr bar than in the other three bars, where σ_gb shows similar height.
No numeric values are printed on the bars, the data points or the axes beyond the y-axis tick labels 0-1400.
The caption states the figure is a schematic of the yield strengths measured by tensile tests together with the calculated yield strengths produced by the four mechanisms.
The citing text asserts the calculated and experimental yield strengths are in very good agreement and that solution strengthening is evidently the primary strengthening mechanism for these samples.

The citing text states that precipitation strengthening also plays a significant role, with Ni and Cr acting synergistically to increase precipitate size and thus gradually raise the precipitation contribution.

subfigures.description: Stacked bar chart of calculated yield-strength contributions (σ_0 orange, σ_gb green, σ_ss purple, σ_prep yellow) for the samples 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr, overlaid with brown spheres marking the experimental (tensile-tested) yield strength for each sample. Axes: x = sample, y = Yield strength (MPa), 0-1400 with 200 MPa ticks.

unreadable_items: No numeric labels are printed on individual stacked segments or on the experimental markers, so per-mechanism and measured yield-strength values cannot be read exactly from the image.
